notes: The sheet is an upright handwritten mathematical manuscript: 15 prose baselines, five numbered display baselines, and two lower definition/identification rows (22 in the stated line count), plus the separate lower-left folio 79. No diagram, drawing, or insertion leader occurs. The opening continues a previous sentence; no missing initial opening parenthesis is supplied. The page discusses the normalizer extension (13), its class in degree-two cohomology, the K(pi,1) comparison and a Kummer sequence, followed by an inverse-limit sequence and the beginning of an unfinished case distinction. The two cancellations are local: after élément, and over the car-like group on the final baseline. The final abbreviation is live and is not crossed by that cancellation. Every word and formula on both halves was read; all substantive witness discrepancies and C-mark candidates received the recorded crops, with no recrop. The subscript n in (16) is independently supported by the explicit local definition below (17). The small angled mark below that lower inverse-limit arrow is the grave accent of the next-line où, not a new index. The notation comparisons were checked locally; the page's claims about existence of splittings, cohomology comparison and passage to inverse limits were not proved or extended. In particular the exactness assertion was not used to force an arrowhead where the ink is weak. E is written consistently as a rounded two-lobed cursive letter, with no contrasting roman E on this page; C E versus H mathcal E is treated as editorial alphabet styling. G_m likewise remains in C's notation rather than being changed to H's blackboard font. No authorial top page number is present. The narrow bottom-left 79 is kept as a margin numeral, not asserted to be the author's page numbering. The nested C doubts in deleted de and car. were not listed among the supplied M1220-M1222 marks; both remain unresolved and are explicitly listed below.
